description: Verify that with two competing DHCP servers on the same interface, DUT silently discards SERVER-1's mismatched-xid OFFER and selects SERVER-2 — the resulting REQUEST carries Option 54 = SERVER-2's identifier (RFC 2131 §3.1)
approach:
[Objective]
TC8 §4.7.3 Topology 3 puts two server emuls on a single DUT interface (NOT multi-iface — that's USAGE_01). Two server emuls fire on Listening_for_request entry; SERVER-1 emits an OFFER with xid_offset = +1 (mismatched, must be silently dropped per INIT_ALLOC_04 logic), SERVER-2 emits with xid_offset = 0 and a distinct server_id (kSecondServerIdBe). DUT selects SERVER-2 and the subsequent REQUEST's Option 54 echoes SERVER-2's id.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. DUT → wire: DHCPDISCOVER.
2. SERVER-1 → DUT: DHCPOFFER (xid mismatched).
3. SERVER-2 → DUT: DHCPOFFER (xid match, server_id = S2).
4. DUT → wire: DHCPREQUEST
   • Option 54 == S2   ← key check

[Pass condition]
REQUEST.Option54 equals SERVER-2's identifier.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_no_discover / Fail_no_request — DORA missing
• Fail_request_selected_mismatched_server — DUT picked SERVER-1 (via the mismatched-xid OFFER) instead

verdicts.Fail_no_discover: No DUT DHCPDISCOVER within the listen window
verdicts.Fail_request_selected_mismatched_server: DUT DHCPREQUEST did not select the second server
